headline: Meta launches Muse Spark Open, most capable US open-weight model for Macs
summary: The new AI model is optimized for Mac Studio, but requires a hefty 1TB of RAM to run.
details: Meta has unveiled Muse Spark Open, an open-weight AI model designed to run on Apple's Mac Studio hardware. The company claims it is the "most capable US open-weight model to date."
While optimized for Macs, the model has significant hardware requirements, needing a massive 1TB of RAM to operate effectively. This makes it inaccessible for most consumer-grade Macs.

The release positions Meta as a key player in the open-source AI community, providing powerful tools for researchers and developers. The model's performance on Mac hardware is expected to be a point of interest for the Apple developer ecosystem.
caption:
Meta's new AI model, Muse Spark Open, is now available for Mac Studio users.

Meta has unveiled Muse Spark Open, an open-weight AI model designed to run on Apple's Mac Studio hardware. The company claims it is the "most capable US open-weight model to date."

While optimized for Macs, the model has significant hardware requirements, needing a massive 1TB of RAM to operate effectively. This makes it inaccessible for most consumer-grade Macs.

The release positions Meta as a key player in the open-source AI community, providing powerful tools for researchers and developers. The model's performance on Mac hardware is expected to be a point of interest for the Apple developer ecosystem.

topic: governments use zero-click spyware via online ads
headline_marked: Governments use [[online ads]] to deliver zero-click spyware, Citizen Lab reports
headline: Governments use online ads to deliver zero-click spyware, Citizen Lab reports
summary: An Israeli firm's ad platform is reportedly being used by spyware makers to target devices globally with undetectable malware, marking a new escalation in cyber-espionage.
details: Security researchers at The Citizen Lab have revealed that government spyware developers are leveraging global advertising networks to hack devices. An Israeli company, Discover-Tech, allegedly provides a platform that acts as a conduit between ad vendors and the spyware industry, enabling targeted attacks.

The report indicates that at least two major zero-click spyware makers, Candiru and Bindecy, have utilized Discover-Tech's advertising platform. These spyware tools are designed to infect devices without requiring the victim to click a link or open a message, making them particularly insidious.

One documented attack utilized Candiru's spyware to compromise at least 45 Windows computers at Al Jazeera in 2024 and 2025. These devices were reportedly infected through online advertisements embedded with malicious code, highlighting the real-world impact of this tactic.

While the specific governments behind these attacks remain unclear, this is the first confirmed instance of zero-click government-backed spyware being delivered via online advertisements. This method poses a significant risk to a vast number of devices worldwide.

Discover-Tech's platform, named Controlium, had its source code exposed on login pages, allowing researchers to reconstruct its control panel. This dashboard appears to be built for pushing malicious content to targeted users alongside regular advertisements.

Further investigation by Citizen Lab uncovered exposed user login records for the Controlium dashboard and billions of ad bidding records. These records showed that Discover-Tech's ads were displayed across tens of thousands of websites and mobile apps, reaching devices used by militaries, governments, and critical infrastructure agencies.
